problems.description: Convention score 0.68 is driven by 27 pre-existing violations in files this commit did NOT touch (celery_app.py, celery_config.py, __init__.py) — PascalCase classes, snake_case functions, module constants — so they predate and are not attributable to this diff; unaddressed here.

Moving init_db() to module import time adds a side-effect-on-import (runs on every import, including in the test fixture which calls it again explicitly); acceptable for a small Flask app but a mild smell.
tests/test_app.py relies on a sys.path.insert(0, ...) hack to import app; works but fragile to test layout changes.

strengths: Fixes a real bug: new tasks were inserted with status 'done' instead of 'pending'
Comprehensive tests cover validation errors (missing/blank/no body), the full task lifecycle, ordering, and 404s
Removes genuinely dead code: unused legacy helper, unwired notification stub, and a backward-compat alias
Tests isolate the DB cleanly via tmp_path + monkeypatch fixture
commit_reviews.summary: A clean greenfield-session commit that fixes the create_task status bug, strips dead legacy code, and adds thorough test coverage — the low 0.68 convention score reflects pre-existing violations in untouched files (celery_app.py/celery_config.py/__init__.py), not anything this diff introduced.

problems.description: SECRET_KEY falls back to a hardcoded 'dev-secret-key-change-in-production' when the env var is unset; tokens minted with the known default would be forgeable if deployed without configuration.

Measured convention score is 0.68 with 27 violations, but the flagged files (celery_app.py, celery_config.py, __init__.py) are outside this commit's +2-file diff; the violations appear to be pre-existing worktree state rather than introduced here. The app.py changes themselves use snake_case functions and UPPER_CASE constants correctly.
/auth/login has no rate limiting or attempt throttling, leaving credential guessing unbounded.

Auth adds roughly 150 lines to an already-single-file app (now models for both users and tasks plus auth routes); the file continues to grow, though splitting would break the established single-file baseline pattern.

strengths: Passwords hashed with werkzeug generate_password_hash/check_password_hash rather than stored in plaintext
Owner scoping applied consistently across get/update/delete task queries (WHERE owner_id = ?), preventing cross-user access (IDOR)
Migration adds owner_id as a nullable column via PRAGMA inspection, preserving existing rows instead of dropping or rewriting data
login_required decorator uses functools.wraps, Bearer-token parsing, and uniform 401 JSON responses; JWT exp is timezone-aware
Duplicate-username handling done both pre-checked and via sqlite3.IntegrityError catch
Follows the existing single-file structure: get_db context manager, comment-section headers, function-based models
commit_reviews.summary: A well-scoped Session 2 feature that adds JWT auth and user-scoped task ownership cleanly inside the existing single-file Flask structure, with proper hashing, consistent owner scoping, and a data-preserving migration — the low convention score traces to pre-existing violations outside this commit's diff.

problems.description: app.py imports `send_notification_email` from tasks at module load, which pulls in the full celery_app -> celery_config chain; importing the Flask app now requires Celery (and its broker deps) installed even for requests that never touch notifications.

create_user silently fabricates the email `{username}@example.com` when none is supplied, then stores it as real data; that fake address will later be 'emailed' on task completion with no way to distinguish it from a genuine one.

Email dispatch is a fire-and-forget side effect inside the edit_task request handler; acceptable as a story-level integration, but the route now hard-couples to the notification transport rather than going through an injected seam.

Discrepancy with mechanical score: most of the 27 flagged violations are false positives or inherent to the pattern — celery_config.py module-level settings (broker_url, result_backend) must be lowercase to satisfy Celery's config-from-object API, and celery_app.py/app.py contain no actual classes or functions to rename; the __init__.py function violations are pre-existing, not introduced here.

strengths: Clean component split (celery_app / celery_config / tasks) that explicitly exists to avoid circular imports between the Flask app and the worker.
The _migrate_add_email migration faithfully mirrors the existing _migrate_add_owner_id pattern (PRAGMA check + nullable ALTER), preserving existing users instead of rewriting data.
just_completed correctly detects the state transition (previous status != 'completed') and is defensively guarded against missing owner/email via get_user_by_id None checks.
Comprehensive new test suite with fixtures (tmp_path DATABASE override, mocked .delay) consistent with the codebase's testing style.
commit_reviews.summary: A well-structured Celery-based notification integration that fits the story arc and codebase conventions well; the mechanical convention score of 0.68 understates true adherence because most violations are false positives intrinsic to Celery's config API or pre-existing files.

problems.description: Dead delegation wrapper `get_user_by_username` left in app.py:116 — routes were rewired to `user_repo.get_by_username` directly, so the wrapper is now unreferenced leftover code from the refactor.

BaseRepository.create/update accept untyped `**fields`, and `table_name: str = None` mismatches its actual None default (should be `str | None`) — the new abstraction is looser-typed than the direct code it replaced.
`datetime` import reordered to `timedelta, timezone, datetime` — cosmetic churn unrelated to the refactor that adds diff noise.
No test evidence in the commit; a data-layer refactor of this breadth should be verified against the story's pytest suite (test_executed_success not shown).

strengths: Behavior-preserving repository extraction — route handlers now delegate to a dedicated data layer instead of inline SQL.
Clean package layout: `repositories/__init__.py` with `__all__` exports, abstract base + per-table subclasses.
DRY'd shared plumbing (generic `get_by_id`/`list_all`/`delete`) and removed the now-unused `generate_password_hash` import.
Consistent `dict | None` type hints on new public signatures; new repo files themselves follow snake_case/PascalCase conventions.
commit_reviews.summary: A solid, behavior-preserving repository-pattern refactor with clean package structure — only minor debt (a dead wrapper, loose `**fields` typing) — and the measured convention violations (0.68) sit mostly in untouched celery files, not in the new code.

problems.description: Introduces a hard new runtime dependency on Redis (RATELIMIT_STORAGE_URI defaults to redis://localhost:6379/1) for Flask-Limiter storage. The app was previously self-contained on SQLite; it now fails to start without a real Redis, and the sandbox has none.

tests/conftest.py globally monkeypatches redis.from_url at import time to force fakeredis. This mutates a third-party module globally and leaks beyond the suite; it is a symptom of the limiter's storage URI not being injectable rather than a clean solution.
GET /tasks response shape changes from a bare list to {data, next_cursor, total} with no versioning or back-compat, breaking any existing client of the endpoint.
rate_limit_key() re-decodes the JWT on every request in addition to login_required's decode (double verification per authenticated request), and a COUNT(*) scan runs on every page request.
Ordering on the existing endpoint changes from created_at DESC to id DESC. Equivalent under monotonic ids and well documented in a comment, but still a subtle semantic change to prior behavior.

strengths: Cursor-based pagination with a stable, indexable id cursor, clamped and validated limit, and has_more/next_cursor semantics — implemented cleanly in the repository layer.
Rate limiting keyed per-user with an IP fallback for anonymous traffic and a JSON 429 handler — a sound security design that bounds both authenticated and unauthenticated load.
Well-documented rationale (ordering comment, conftest docstring), type hints on public signatures, and snake_case/UPPER_CASE naming throughout the new code.
Existing tests updated for the new response envelope and new pagination tests added; the autouse fixture isolates rate-limit state per test.
commit_reviews.summary: A net-positive session that adds clean cursor pagination and per-user rate limiting with tests and documentation, but at the cost of a new hard Redis runtime dependency and an import-time fakeredis monkeypatch — and the 0.68 convention score reflects pre-existing violations in untouched files (celery_app.py, celery_config.py, __init__.py), not this diff, whose own code is convention-compliant.
